testCases.input: In this tutorial we're going to walk through the two-pointer technique for solving array problems in JavaScript. The idea is simple: instead of using nested loops which cost you O(n squared) time, you place one pointer at the start of a sorted array and another at the end. On each step you look at the sum of the two values. If the sum is too small, you move the left pointer forward to increase it. If the sum is too large, you move the right pointer backward to decrease it. You keep narrowing the window until the pointers meet or you find the target pair. This turns an O(n squared) brute force search into a single O(n) pass, which matters a lot once your input arrays get large.
testCases.notes: Single, well-scoped concept in a common language. Baseline should complete cleanly here too.
